brief: A seven-cell honeycomb work surface, covered on top, with every open outside edge finished with caps.

requirements.requirement: Seven-cell honeycomb work surface: one centre cell with six surrounding cells in a flower layout, all on one level.
requirements.evidence: Hex base Full pieces at (0,0), (1,0), (1,-1), (0,-1), (-1,0), (-1,1), (0,1), all level 0. Six joint bolts lock the six spokes to the centre cell.
Seven top covers (addCover, face top), one on each of the seven cells.

requirements.requirement: Every open outside edge finished with caps.
requirements.evidence: 18 caps (addCap, face *) on the six outer cells, three per cell at the outward-facing bearings. The centre cell has no open edges. Check reports no issues and meshClash clear.

finish.summary: Built a seven-cell flower of Hex base Full pieces on level 0, with a top cover on each cell, 18 caps on the outer open edges, and six joint bolts on the centre spokes to clear the loose-body warning. check_build returns ok, no issues, meshClash clear. I did not add joint bolts on the rim-to-rim joints; the centre spokes are enough to clear the warning.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
